name: sdlc-diagnose-failures
description: Diagnose a reproducible software failure when the owning boundary or root cause is unclear, especially when the error is distant from its trigger.
---

# Diagnose a software failure

1. Capture the smallest available reproduction. Record the input or state, expected behavior, observed behavior, and error location. If you cannot reproduce it, separate reported evidence from observations and state the missing prerequisite.
2. Compare the failing path with a known-good path where available. Trace the relevant data or state upstream from the symptom until you locate the first unexpected change and the boundary that owns it.
3. If more than one cause fits, choose a narrowly scoped observation that would distinguish the leading explanations. Use existing checks or temporary local instrumentation without logging sensitive values. Change one variable at a time; don't keep speculative fixes or temporary instrumentation.
4. Fix the evidenced cause at its owning boundary. Verify the original reproduction and nearby behavior after the change. For diagnosis-only tasks, stop at the evidence and proposed next check instead of editing production code.

Use the repository's existing tooling and the session's permissions. Do not fetch or run external scripts to complete this workflow.
